parameters.value: Lowell Observatory 24-inch Clark refractor (Flagstaff, 2210 m)
quotes: The large refractor for which the spectrograph was designed and with which it is used has an objective, by Clarks
parameters.note: Slipher 1917 (S17, p. 404): "The spectrograph was attached to the 24-inch refractor."

quotes: clear aper- ture of 61 cm and a focal length of 983 cm for the photographic rays
parameters.note: Visual-rays focal length not stated. A color-curve of the objective is in Fig. 1 of S04 (not digitized).

quotes: focal length of 983 cm for the photographic rays
This ratio of aperture to focus-1 to 16
parameters.note: DERIVED: 983/61 = f/16.1; plate scale 9830 mm / 206264.8 = 47.66 um per arcsec = 20.98 arcsec per mm at the slit.

parameters.value: 95 mm doublet (light flint + light crown, cemented) 1.422 m inside the 4400 A focus, unites the photographic rays near 4400 A on the slit plate; used for stellar and planetary work. Use for the nebular plates NOT STATED (not used for the Pleiades plate of 1912)
quotes: It has an aperture of 95 mm and is placed 1.422 m inside the focus of X 4400
The lens is a doublet made of a double convex lens of a special light flint from Mantois
parameters.note: S12 (p. 26): "(No cor- recting lens was used.)" for the 1912 Pleiades-nebula plate. For an extended source the slit illumination does not depend on the focus (S13, p. 56: "The collimator must of course fit the telescope"), so the preset omits it.

quotes: gave the collimator a focal length 1.2683 times that of the camera, or 489.1 mm
the focal length of the visual lens was 491.3 mm
parameters.note: Measured in the laboratory by Slipher (Schuster method + iron negative); "about 490 mm" on p. 2 and in S05 p. 318.

quotes: This gave the lens an aperture of 30.5 mm
There are two collimation lenses, each having an aperture of
parameters.note: DERIVED: 489.1/30.5 = f/16.04, matching the objective (f/16.1). Collimator type: lens (cemented doublet, Mantois crown and flint, Hastings design: S04 p. 10, "a doublet lately designed by Dr. Hastings").

parameters.value: Transmissive lens collimator behind the slit; slit and refractor beam are on axis; no obscuration, no fold
quotes: The collimator and slit-plate may be moved as a whole in this sleeve through 70 mm by a rack and pinion
The jaws are of speculum metal and are highly polished
parameters.note: On-axis/off-axis gate: NOT APPLICABLE (a lens collimator in line with the refractor tube, the slit at the objective focus; nothing stands in a returning beam). The speculum jaws reflect the slit-stopped light sideways into a guiding tube (S04 p. 6), outside the cone.

parameters.value: Symmetric jaws opened by a wedge and screw of 0.25 mm pitch, head in ten parts: 0.025 mm per division; separate jaws below the slit set the spectrum width
quotes: The screw has a pitch of 0.25 mm and a milled head divided into ten equal parts
one division, corresponds to a slit-width of 0.025 mni
Just beneath the slit is a pair of jaws for controlling the width of the spectra
With a slit- width of 0.02 mm, which is the width generally used
parameters.note: Stellar and planetary work with the three-prism train. DERIVED: 0.02 mm = 0.42 arcsec on the sky.

parameters.unit: mm ("equivalent slit-width"; read as the slit image on the plate)
quotes: The equivalent slit-width is usually about .06 mm
parameters.note: Transcribed from the scan (p. 405). Slipher gave no other slit width for the nebulae (S13 says only "a wider slit"). Thompson (T13, p. 4) reads it as the projected width on the plate. DERIVED on that reading: slit = 0.06 mm x (489.1/82.55) = 0.355 mm = 7.46 arcsec on the sky (T13 quotes 8.25 arcsec, factor unstated; see Conflicts). 0.06 mm x 140 A/mm = 8.4 A.

parameters.value: about 4 arcmin (Pleiades-nebula plates, 1912); 11.4 mm at the slit (DERIVED)
quotes: The slit having a length of about four minutes of arc was oriented east and west
parameters.note: Transcribed from the scan. DERIVED: 240 arcsec x 47.66 um/arcsec = 11.4 mm; projected 11.4 x 82.55/489.1 = 1.93 mm: the spectrum width on the plate (INFERRED; the nebular-plate width is not stated).

quotes: using a very dense 64-degree prism
parameters.note: Transcribed from the scan. S17 (p. 404): "The dispersion piece of the spectrograph has generally been a 64 degrees prism of dense glass". S17B (p. 60): "two 64 deg.5 prisms" for NGC 1068. These are NOT the 60 deg single prisms of S04 (59 deg 59' 50" flint, 59 deg 59' 30" crown); they were added after 1904.

parameters.value: 1 prism for most nebulae; 2 prisms for two nebulae of the 1917 list and for the 1917 NGC 1068 plate
quotes: The dispersion piece of the spectrograph has generally been a 64° prism of dense glass, but for two of the nebulæ a dispersion of two 64° prisms was used
parameters.note: Transcribed from the scan. S17B (p. 60): "under the higher dispersion of two 64 deg.5 prisms ... An exposure was made from November 12 to 16, 1917, with a duration of thirty-five hours." Which two nebulae in the list: NOT FOUND.

parameters.value: NOT FOUND. "very dense"/"dense glass" only. See the glass section: INFERRED dense flint like the 1904 single flint prism (n(Hgamma) = 1.7310); proposed Schott N-SF15
quotes: using a very dense 64-degree prism
parameters.note: No maker, melt, index or Abbe number is published for the 64 deg prism(s). The 1904 single "very dense flint" prism has measured indices (S04 p. 15 Table IV).

parameters.value: NOT FOUND (size, orientation, minimum-deviation setting for the nebulae)
quotes: the prisms have been used set at minimum deviation for wave-length 4415
parameters.note: That line is the stellar three-prism setting of 1905. The nebular setting is not stated; the 140 A/mm "in the violet" is reproduced by a dense flint at minimum deviation near 4400 A (DERIVED below).

parameters.value: 3 prisms, Schott O 102 dense silicate flint, apex 62 deg 52' 56", 62 deg 52' 12", 62 deg 52' 31"; bases 67 mm; path in glass a little over 100 mm; automatic minimum-deviation device; semicircular prism box 13 in diameter
quotes: The glass is a dense silicate flint, the same brand, O 102
The bases are each 67 mm, and the average length of the path of the fight through the glass is slightly more than 100 mm
a prism-train equipped with a mini- mum deviation device
parameters.note: Stellar/planetary configuration (era 1902-1910); total deviation at Hgamma 176 deg 29' (Table I). S05 (p. 318): "a train of three 63o dense flint prisms".

quotes: The average index for H<y is 1.67448, and the total deviation is
parameters.note: Table values transcribed from the scan image (p. 12); the OCR text layer garbles the table. Total deviations 165 deg 22' (Hα), 167 18 (D2), 172 11 (Hβ), 174 41 (4529), 176 29 (Hγ), 179 14 (Hδ), 181 5 (H), 181 38 (K).

parameters.value: apex 59 deg 59' 50"; n: Hα 1.6905, D2 1.6954, Hβ 1.7131, Hγ 1.7310 (top row printed as Hδ 1.7360 is out of line; see Conflicts)
quotes: There are two single prisms, one a very dense flint
parameters.note: Table transcribed from the scan image (p. 15). Dispersion at Hγ: long camera 32 A/mm, short camera 39 A/mm (p. 16: "Long camera, 32 tenth-meters per mm"). Crown prism 59 deg 59' 30": n Hγ 1.6038; 62 A/mm long camera.

parameters.value: Voigtlander commercial photographic lens, focal ratio about 1:2.5, focal length "3 1/4-inch"
quotes: a 3¼-inch Voigtlander camera it is an efficient instrument for nebular work
parameters.note: Transcribed from the scan image (p. 22: "3¼-inch"). S17 (p. 404): "The camera of the Lowell spectrograph has a lens working at a speed ratio of about 1:2.5." T13 (p. 3): "Slipher purchased an f /2.5 commercial camera lens from Voigtlander". DERIVED: 3.25 in = 82.55 mm focal length (reading the inch figure as focal length, INFERRED; consistent with S16: collimator "six times" the camera focal length, 489.1/82.55 = 5.92, and with the "30-fold" speed gain, (471.4/82.55)^2 = 32.6); aperture 82.55/2.5 = 33.0 mm. The lens model (Heliar, Dynar, Collinear, ...) is NOT FOUND.

parameters.value: Replacing the 18.5-inch camera by the 3 1/4-inch Voigtlander increases the speed "fully 30-fold"
quotes: This change of cameras increases the speed of the instrument fully 30-fold
parameters.note: Transcribed from the scan. Slipher to Lowell (SM13, p. 156): about 200 times faster than the three-prism instrument.

parameters.value: "the collimator focus six times that of the camera" (spectrograph with the fast camera, 1916)
quotes: the collimator focus six times that of the camera
parameters.note: DERIVED: 489.1/6 = 81.5 mm, consistent with 3.25 in = 82.55 mm (ratio 5.92). The 1916 plate is a single-prism plate of the same instrument ("single-prism spectrograph of high light- power").

parameters.value: collimated beam 30.5 mm into a 33 mm lens: effective focal ratio f/2.7 (DERIVED)
quotes: This gave the lens an aperture of 30.5 mm
parameters.note: DERIVED: 82.55/30.5 = f/2.71. The spectrograph speed for extended sources is set by this beam, not by the lens aperture, unless the prism at minimum deviation widens it (it does not).

parameters.unit: mm focal length; aperture 36 mm (S04) or 35 mm (S05); 1:13
quotes: Mean /=471.4 mm
This makes the angular aperture of the lens 1:13
There are two camera lenses, each of 36 mm aperture
parameters.note: Brass tube 19 inches long, plate tipped to bring the violet end nearer the lens (p. 11-12). S05 (p. 318): "a camera of 35 mm aperture and 471 mm focus". S15 (p. 22) calls it the "18.5-inch camera" (= 470 mm).

quotes: 385.7 mm for the focal length of the short camera
Its angular aperture is 1 : 11
parameters.note: Brass tube 15 inches long. The 1904 paper says the short camera was used for the stellar plates (exposure times "are for the short camera", p. 17).

parameters.value: brass holders for plates 2 x 3 inches (four holders); an eyepiece substitutes for the holder
quotes: hold plates of size 2 by 3 inches
parameters.note: Plate size for the Voigtlander nebular camera: NOT FOUND (T13 Fig. 1: holder "held under two mounting screws").

parameters.unit: A per mm ("in the violet of the spectrum")
quotes: The linear dispersion of the spectra is about 140 tenth-meters per millimeter in the violet of the spectrum
parameters.note: Transcribed from the scan (p. 405). Slipher gives no wavelength; the violet is the F-H region he measured (S13: "from F to H"). T13 (p. 4): "his prism worked at 140 A mm-1". Plate scale of the whole camera: 1/(140 A/mm). DERIVED angular dispersion: 206265/(82.55 x 140) = 17.8 arcsec per A.

quotes: The linear dispersion for the two cameras at different points
parameters.note: Table values transcribed from the scan image. S05 (p. 319), min deviation 4415, long camera: 4250 9.9; 4300 10.6; 4350 11.4; 4400 12.3; 4450 13.2; 4500 14.1; 4550 15.0 A/mm.

parameters.value: F to H (about 4861 to 3968 A) measured; length about 6.7 mm on the plate (INFERRED)
quotes: The measures extended over the region of spectrum from F to H
parameters.note: INFERRED length: S16 says the spectrum length is "forty times the equivalent slit-width" (a single-prism plate with the 6:1 ratio); a 1 mm slit images to 1/5.92 = 0.169 mm; 40 x 0.169 = 6.75 mm; x 140 A/mm = 945 A, matching F-H (893 A). The range actually exposed (S/N falls to the red and violet end) is NOT stated.

parameters.value: sharpest solar negatives (three-prism train): 0.11 A at Hδ, 0.16 A at 4300, 0.22 A at 4500; lines separated no closer than 0.25 A at Hγ on most rapid plates in the brightest stars
quotes: the solar spectrum is about 0.11 tenth-meters at Hh
lines are not separated at Ht which
differ in wave-length by much less than 0.25 tenth-meters
parameters.note: Stellar-era limit (slit 0.02 mm, 11 A/mm). DERIVED plate limit: 0.25 A / 11.4 A/mm = 0.022 mm. For the nebular plates the 0.06 mm slit image is about three times larger; no nebular line width or resolving limit is published (NOT FOUND).

parameters.value: Seed "30" plates (nebular work, 1915); Seed 23 and Seed 27 (stellar, 1905); sensitizing dyes and baths experimented with
quotes: Seed 30 plates were
parameters.note: Transcribed from the scan. S05 (p. 319): "no better on Seed 23 plates than it should be on the coarser 27 emulsion". SM13 (p. 155-156 text): Slipher tried "different kinds of photographic plates and even dyes". Grain size and speed: NOT FOUND.

parameters.value: iron-vanadium spark (nebular work); iron spark (stellar); spark exposed several times during the long nebular exposure
quotes: The iron-vanadium spark comparison spectrum is exposed a
parameters.note: Transcribed from the scan. S15 (p. 22): "The comparison spectrum was iron and vanadium."

parameters.value: constant-temperature case, electrically heated; prism-box temperature held to 0.1-0.2 C per night
quotes: the temperature does not change more than
parameters.note: S17: "The spectrograph is electrically maintained at a constant temperature".

parameters.value: Hartmann spectrocomparator, 15 diameters, a similar plate of Saturn (G-type) as velocity standard; later nebular spectra superposed on a standard dark-line spectrum
quotes: These spectrograms were measured with the Hartmann spectrocomparator
parameters.note: Transcribed from the scan.

parameters.value: refractor focus -> slit plate -> collimator (489 mm) -> three prisms in minimum deviation (total deviation ~176 deg, camera nearly beside the collimator) -> camera lens near the third prism -> plate; camera above or below the collimator (spectrograph rotates about the optical axis)
quotes: It permits the spectroscope to be turned so that
the camera is either above or below the collimator
The camera tube screws into the prism-box mechanism, with the lens near the third prism
parameters.note: MEASURED/SOURCED: deviations of Table I. Guiding: a Huggins device (light stopped by the speculum jaws) and a Vogel device (light reflected from the first prism face).

parameters.value: collimated beam leaves the collimator upward/downward through the prism (on a plate with a triangular cover); the Voigtlander lens in a large brass cylinder stands at an angle to the collimator axis; the plate holder sits at the lens focus
quotes: The collimated beam from the Brashear spectrograph enters from below
parameters.note: Fig. 1 of T13 is a photograph without a scale or dimensions. The beam deviation is DERIVED: a 64 deg prism of nHgamma 1.73 at minimum deviation turns the beam by 68.9 deg (the camera axis is therefore 68.9 deg from the collimator axis, not ~176 deg as in the three-prism train). Collimator-to-prism and prism-to-camera distances: NOT FOUND (SCHEMATIC).

parameters.value: Sep 17 1912: 6 h 50 min (single 64 deg prism); Nov 15-16: two nights; Dec 3-4: two nights; Dec 29-30-31: three nights; total about four plates
quotes: was exposed for 6 hours and 50 minutes, on September
November 15-16
parameters.note: Transcribed from the scan. T13 (p. 4): the first M31 plate was "one full night".

parameters.value: 1917 list: "generally from twenty to forty hours", sometimes weeks; NGC 1068: 6.5 h (1913), about 13 h (1913), 35 h with two 64.5 deg prisms (Nov 12-16 1917); Pleiades nebula 5.25 h and 21 h (1912); rho Oph nebula 20 h (1916, single prism)
